16.0.0.en: Sarai heard God's promise to her husband Abram that He would give him offspring, but ten years had passed for them in the land of Canaan and Sarai had reached the age of 75, so she became sure of her inability to bear children. She thought of giving her maid Hagar to her husband to lie with her, so that if she bore a son he would be counted as the mistress's and not the maid's, according to the custom of that time. Perhaps Sarai thought that the cause of the barrenness was her husband, so that if he lay with another woman and did not beget, she would be sure of that and not be the cause.

16.1.0.en: Abram obeyed his wife's advice, not to fulfil a desire but in an attempt to fulfil God's promise by a human method and to obtain offspring, and he did not ask God about this. His obedience to Sarai was an error, because he sought with her a human means to fulfil God's promise, as if God were unable to fulfil His promises; and in spite of his friendship with God he neglected prayer and consulting Him in this matter. Perhaps he tried to please his wife, but he should have obeyed God more than his wife.

16.2.0.en: Sarai gave Hagar her maid to her husband, and at that time polygamy and union with maidservants were permitted, and Abram's self-restraint appears in that it was Sarai who pushed him to it. When he lay with her she conceived, and she became proud toward her mistress, since she was distinguished from her by the ability to bear children, and she began to look at her mistress with contempt, which distressed Sarai greatly.

16.2.1.en: If God gives you gifts and distinguishes you above others, do not be proud, for the gift is from Him and not from you, and hasten to thank Him if He gives you in spite of your many sins and does not give to others who are better than you. In this way you keep your humility and secure God's gifts to you.

16.3.0.en: Sarai suffered greatly from her sense of helplessness before her maid, and then realized that the problem of not bearing children was her own responsibility and not her husband's. But this did not move her to repent of relying on her own reason to fulfil God's purposes; rather she accused her husband of wronging her, although it was she who had wronged him by marrying him to Hagar, and she asked God to vindicate her right and discipline her husband, for she said, "The Lord judge between me and you." As for Abram, he bore it in silence, making allowance for her because of her sense of helplessness, and he did not reproach her.

16.4.0.en: Abram gave Sarai the freedom to do with Hagar what she wished, because the latter had become proud, and it was her mistress's right to discipline her for that. But Sarai disciplined her severely, to the point of humiliation, either with many tasks or with bad treatment, so that Hagar could not bear it and fled from the house, although she was pregnant and in need of care and rest. Perhaps Hagar felt that her mistress was wearying her with work beyond her strength that could cause the loss of the child, so she fled.

16.5.s.en: (2) Hagar's flight and the birth of Ishmael

16.5.1.en: The way to Shur: it is the caravan road in the wilderness.

16.5.2.en: In her flight Hagar headed to the wilderness of Paran, north of Sinai, and perhaps she was returning to Egypt, her original country, and was heading for the way to Shur, a well-known road traveled by caravans. She rested at a spring of water, perhaps the Springs of Moses, and the angel of the Lord appeared to her, and perhaps it was a divine appearance, as evidenced by the fact that she afterwards addressed him as God.

16.6.0.en: The angel of the Lord called her Sarai's maid to declare to her her natural position, for her place was Sarai's house and not flight, and he asked her, "Where are you going?" and she confessed that she was fleeing from her mistress's harshness toward her.

16.7.0.en: The angel asked her not to flee but to return to her mistress Sarai and submit to her, because she had erred by her pride when she conceived, and for this reason Sarai humbled her; so she must return and behave submissively toward her mistress as she used to behave in former times before she conceived.

16.8.0.en: God comforted her because she was humbled, and it seems she asked for His help, so He promised her a son, "Ishmael," that is, God has heard her, and He also promised her abundant offspring from him.

16.8.1.en: God hears you when you are in distress and call on Him, and He keeps you, blesses you and guides you to your good. And if He asks of you the opposite of what you wished, submit to His will so that you find rest.

16.9.0.en: He prophesied that Ishmael would be fierce in temper like the wild beasts, attacking those around him to dominate them, and others would rise against him and wrong him as he wrongs them. He also determined the dwelling place of him and his seed, that it would be before his brothers, that is, the seed of Isaac, and indeed the seed of Ishmael settled in the Arabian Peninsula, facing the land of Canaan in which the seed of Isaac and Jacob settled.

16.10.0.en: You are El Roi: You are the God whom I have seen.

16.10.1.en: Hagar declared that she had seen God at the spring of water, so the well was called Beer-lahai-roi, that is, the living God appeared in this place. This well lies between the city of Kadesh, which means holy and is south of Jerusalem, and Bered, which means cold and lies west of Kadesh.

16.11.0.en: Hagar returned and submitted to her mistress Sarai, who received her, and the days of her pregnancy were completed and she bore a son, and Abram called him Ishmael as God had declared.

16.12.0.en: Abram's age when Ishmael was born was 86 years, and he begot Isaac at the age of one hundred, so Ishmael is fourteen years older than Isaac.

17.0.0.en: God's appearances to Abram follow one another, and covenants between them are repeated, to confirm his faith and that of all his seed. Adam in Paradise had no need of covenants, since he moved freely in love and friendship with God; but after the fall man needed covenants and signs, such as the rainbow in the days of Noah and circumcision for Abraham, so that he might stand firm in his faith and not be shaken by the evil surrounding him.

17.0.1.en: Abram reached the age of 99 years and the fulfilment of God's promise of offspring drew near, so God appeared to him to prepare him spiritually, declaring Himself to be Almighty, for He is able to do everything, even what surpasses reason, namely that Sarah should bear a child at the age of ninety.

17.0.2.en: Walk before Me: that you may know that I care for you and so be reassured, and that I watch over you and so live in My fear and keep away from evil. Be perfect: walk in the way of perfection so as to please Me in all your thoughts, words and deeds.

17.0.3.en: Remember always that God sees you and cares for you, so do not be troubled by the evils around you or the afflictions that can harm you, for He is able to protect you even if you enter into affliction, and if you fall, He raises you up. Remember in all your dealings that God is with you, so do not anger Him, and likewise in your times alone, so that you keep your mind and all your senses pure.

17.1.0.en: Walking in the way of perfection is the condition for receiving the divine covenant and the abundant blessing in offspring.

17.2.0.en: Abram felt the greatness of God Almighty and His kindnesses and surpassing love, so he prostrated himself in reverence to Him, in thanksgiving for His love and in asking for His help so that he might be able to walk in the way of perfection. And since he submitted, God declared His readiness for more abundant blessings, and God continued His speech with him.

17.3.0.en: Along with the promise of blessing and circumcision, God changed his name from Abram, that is, exalted father, to Abraham, that is, father of a great multitude. For every person loves his name and the meaning of the name affects him, and for this reason one who receives a priestly rank has his name changed, and many prefer to give new names to their children when they receive the sacrament of Baptism, as a declaration of the new blessing they receive. Thus Abraham becomes the father of all believers until the end of the world.

17.4.0.en: God promised an abundance of offspring and the formation of many nations or states that live by Abraham's faith and have kings and rulers from his seed over them.

17.5.0.en: God pledges to be a God and shepherd not only to Abraham but to everyone of his seed who lives in the faith, and this care continues not only in the world but forever in the Kingdom of Heaven.

17.6.0.en: He completed His promise to Abraham to give his seed the land of Canaan, and this was accomplished by Joshua, and this land was a type of the heavenly Jerusalem, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven.

17.7.0.en: Abram was given the sign of the covenant, which is the circumcision of every male, himself and his seed and all who live with him. God wanted the sign to be in the body of man throughout his life so that he would not forget his covenant with God. The cutting of a part of a man's flesh means cutting evil out of his life, to live pure with God in a faith that differs from that of all the people around him, that is, the pagans of that time.

17.7.1.en: God wanted this cutting to be in the reproductive organ, which shares with God in begetting offspring and giving them life, so that man would remember that his life has become new in God, and would also care for his children when he circumcises them into the new life with God.

17.7.2.en: Every male is circumcised and not the females, because the woman is sanctified in the man, so the circumcision of the man includes the covenant with the woman also. This is not to belittle her, for He took care to circumcise the servants, who are of course no better than their mistresses. It is also known that the circumcision of a man is beneficial to health, whereas the circumcision of a woman is harmful.

17.8.0.en: Here the details of carrying out circumcision are declared, and they are:

17.8.1.en: 1- A son of eight days: the time of circumcision is fixed, the eighth day after the child's birth. The number (8) is the day of Christ's Resurrection, which came after the Sabbath, the seventh day, and the Resurrection is the new life; likewise circumcision is a type of Baptism, for it too is the beginning of the new life with God, and for this reason the Church is keen on the baptism of infants.

17.8.2.en: 2- Born in the house: the servants born in the house, who are strangers not of the seed of the head of the household.

17.8.3.en: 3- Bought with your money: the servants who are bought and are circumcised after their purchase; that is, all servants are circumcised, whether after being bought or as their sons whom they beget inside the house. This means God's covenant and care for the poor as for the rich, or for the despised as for the great, for God is Father of all.

17.8.4.en: 4- An everlasting covenant: circumcision is a type of Baptism, which gives us eternal life with God.

17.9.0.en: If a person refuses to be circumcised, he rejects the covenant with God, that is, he is dead in God's sight and has no new life; and to show this, God commanded that he be cut off and removed from the people of God, that is, that he not become a Jew.

17.9.1.en: Remember at the beginning of each day the sacrament of Baptism which you received, so that you may live with your new nature with God, cling to Him and offer your love to everyone you meet.

17.10.0.en: With the covenant of circumcision God changed the name of Sarai, that is, my princess, to Sarah, that is, princess, for she is not a princess to Abram only but a mother of all believers, so she is called a princess in general.

17.11.0.en: It is declared here openly that Sarah will bear a son although her age had reached 89 years, and He even promises that her seed will become very numerous and that nations and states with kings will be formed from it.

17.12.0.en: Abraham rejoiced greatly and prostrated himself on the ground, thanking God for the second time in the same meeting.

17.12.1.en: His laughter here was not doubt but joy and glorification of God's miraculous work, as evidenced by the fact that God did not reproach him as He did Sarah when she laughed (ch. 18:13), and this is confirmed by the faith of the Apostle Paul in (Rom 4:18-20).

17.12.2.en: Thank God for His gifts and submit to Him by prostration, and His heart will rejoice and He will give you more and more, that you may enjoy His fatherhood. Thank Him every morning and in every prayer.

17.13.0.en: Abraham felt the greatness of the divine promise and that he did not deserve it, and he was still attached to his son Ishmael and thought the promise would be fulfilled in him, so he asked God to bless him that he might live before Him, that is, live in God's way and fear.

17.14.0.en: God made allowance for Abraham, because he was the first person in history with whom this miracle happened, of begetting from his aged wife of ninety years. So God was long-suffering toward him and assured him that the promise would be fulfilled through Sarah with offspring, and He fixed the name for him, Isaac, which means laughter, because his parents laughed when they heard the news of his birth, and indeed everyone who heard marveled and rejoiced. And God added in His assurance that He would bless the seed of Isaac and care for them with mercies, not only in this world but forever in the heavenly Kingdom.

17.15.0.en: God also paid heed to Abraham's request for his son Ishmael, that God bless him, so He promised him great offspring, 12 sons; for although he would live far from his father and depart from the faith, the number of his offspring would be great.

17.16.0.en: He returned and affirmed that the promise is of Isaac and not of Ishmael, and fixed the time of his birth a year from that time, that is, when Abraham would be a hundred years old and Sarah ninety, while Ishmael would be 14 years old.

17.17.0.en: God's speech with Abraham ended, with the covenant of circumcision, the changing of names and the promise of Isaac, and then God went up, that is, the appearance in which God had appeared to Abraham vanished. It is not specified here what this appearance was, whether a cloud, a light or some other great sight.

18.0.0.en: After Abraham received the blessing of circumcision, which is a type of Baptism, God appeared to him, for circumcision or Baptism is the beginning of a departure into a new life with God. Abraham was sitting not only to rest but to watch the road, perhaps to do good to a stranger passing by, especially at this time of day when the heat is intense; and the word Mamre, as we said, means vision.

18.1.0.en: Three men: one of the appearances of God the Son in the Old Testament before His incarnation, and with Him two angels. Abraham saw three men from afar passing through the desert, and hurried to them to host them and give them rest in this heat. Here appears Abraham's love of doing good and his haste to it although he was an old man, indeed 99 years old, and his humility also appears in his bowing down to them in respect and honor, although he did not know that they were God and His angels.

18.1.1.en: Care for doing good, for it is your opportunity to offer something to God in the form of the needy, and if you feel that it is offered to God you will hasten to it and humble yourself as you offer your love to them, because it is a great blessing to you which you do not deserve, that God should accept something from you; and you will then rejoice in His love that covers you and satisfies you.

18.2.0.en: Abraham spoke with the one distinguished among the three, whom he afterwards learned was God, and showed him respect when he said, "My Lord," and begged him to accept his hospitality and rest a little at his tent.

18.3.0.en: Abraham begged to perform for them the customary duties of hospitality at that time, namely washing the feet, because they walked in open footwear (sandals) in the sand. This act means love and great humility on the part of this wealthy old man who owned hundreds of servants and very many livestock, and was a great father with a continual relationship with God, yet forgot all this to wash the feet of three men passing in the desert before him.

18.4.0.en: With humility also he asks them, after washing their feet and their resting under the shade of the trees, to let him offer them a little food, which he describes as a morsel of bread, although in truth he would offer a great feast. They agreed and accepted his hospitality and headed toward the tent.

18.5.0.en: A measure: it equals approximately 7.5 liters.

18.5.1.en: Fine meal: the fine white flour.

18.5.2.en: Cakes: bread made on a stone after it is heated with embers, and it is a choice kind of bread.

18.5.3.en: Abraham's love of doing good appears in his haste toward Sarah and his calling her to hurry to prepare the choicest bread, with an ample quantity of flour, three measures. The number three signifies the Holy Trinity, or faith, hope and love.

18.6.0.en: Tender: young, so it is easy to cook and the taste of its meat is delicious.

18.6.1.en: Abraham continued his haste in preparing the feast, so he took a young calf and gave it to one of his servants to slaughter and cook.

18.7.0.en: After the food was prepared he set the meat and bread, and also butter and milk, before his three guests, and he stood, in spite of his old age, to be at their service if they needed anything while they ate. In his humility he did not find himself worthy to eat with them but stood to serve them, and did not assign this work to one of his servants. Of course God and His two angels have no need of material food, but they acted in a miraculous way in eating the food, because it is easy for the spiritual to do the material acts of human beings.

18.7.1.en: Let your giving be generous, as God has given to you generously, for the abundance of your giving expresses the overflow of your love. So care for the needs of others, especially those around you, and give them more than they asked, so that in your giving they feel God, who cares for them more than they ask.

18.8.0.en: The three men spoke, and perhaps what is meant is the great man among them, that is, God, with Abram, and they asked him about Sarah his wife, and he answered that she was in the tent. Perhaps he marveled that they knew his wife's name, Sarah, without his having told them, so he began to understand that they were not ordinary men but spiritual beings from heaven.

18.9.0.en: The time of life: about a year, since life is divided into periods which are years.

18.9.1.en: The great person among the three, who is God, promised Abraham that He would give him offspring from Sarah after about a year. Sarah heard these words, for she was standing inside the tent beside its door, while Abraham was standing in front of the door speaking with the three men.

18.10.0.en: Abraham had reached the age of 99 years and Sarah had reached 89 years, so they were advanced in age and Sarah had lost her ability to bear children, since the custom of women had ceased with her, which shows the ability to bear children.

18.11.0.en: Sarah laughed, either from shame, for how would she conceive when she was old, and what would people say about her; and this is the opinion of St. Clement of Alexandria.

18.11.1.en: St. Augustine, however, says that she laughed with joy at this happy news which she had longed for through many long years. There is a third opinion, that she laughed in doubt about the possibility of conception for an old woman and her aged husband, who had no natural ability to bear children, and this is the more probable opinion. And she said, how shall I have the delight of conceiving at this age, and she humbly called her husband her lord and described him as an old man for whom it is hard to beget.

18.12.0.en: God reproached Abraham because of Sarah's laughter and the weakness of her faith, affirming His ability to fulfil His promise of Sarah's conceiving, because He is able to do everything.

18.13.0.en: Sarah was afraid and lied and said, "I did not laugh," because she did not yet know that it was God; but God affirmed that she had laughed. This shows that the Holy Bible did not hide the weaknesses of the saints, but showed Sarah's sin, so that we the weak may be encouraged, whatever our sins, to live with God and advance in holiness.

18.13.1.en: If Abraham and Sarah offered love in hospitality to strangers, God blessed them with a greater blessing, which was Sarah's conceiving, because God is not indebted to anyone. Trust in God's blessing for you so as to advance in the way of your love for all around you, especially the needy or those fallen into evident sins, to show tenderness to them and encourage them, and then God will have compassion on you.

18.14.0.en: After the talk about Sarah's conceiving, the three men rose and walked on the road to Sodom, and Abraham walked with them to see them off, and this shows his care in completing all the duties of hospitality.

18.15.0.en: God spoke within Himself and said, "Shall I hide from Abraham what I am doing" concerning Sodom and Gomorrah? This shows God's surpassing love for Abraham and His unfathomable humility, to the point of caring for the children of the saints and revealing His secrets to them.

18.15.1.en: For in spite of the vast difference between God and His human creatures, He raises them to the level of friendship, so that He cannot but give them His secrets, and He even accepts their intervention and dialogue with Him in the management of the world ... It is a love that cannot be expressed.

18.15.2.en: God gave reasons for His friendship and His care in revealing His secrets to Abraham, and they are:

18.15.3.en: 1- He will become a great nation, which is the chosen people of God, so he has great value in God's sight.

18.15.4.en: 2- He will be the cause of blessing for all the peoples of the world through Christ, who comes from his seed.

18.15.5.en: 3- Because God has known his faith, his love and his pure conduct, he deserves to be a son of God.

18.15.6.en: 4- So that he may command his seed to love God, worship Him and walk in uprightness.

18.16.0.en: God declared before His angels and before Abraham that the sins of the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah had greatly increased, and through their enormity had become like a cry rising toward heaven.

18.16.3.en: They are two cities lying south of the Dead Sea, and it is understood from the meaning of their two names that they deserve divine punishment by burning and flood.

18.17.0.en: God continued His speech, saying that He had come down from His heaven to examine the two cities and know the extent of their sins and whether they deserved punishment or not, to show His justice in not hastening to judgment but examining well first, to declare the guilt or innocence of every person. God uses human expressions so that we may understand His purposes, such as "come down," but God is present everywhere and does not move from place to place, and He also knows everything and has no need to come down in order to examine.

18.18.0.en: After this part of the talk about Sodom and Gomorrah, the two angels departed and went to Sodom, while Abraham was still standing with the great man whom he now knew with certainty to be God, because He declared His knowledge of the sins of Sodom and that He is the just Judge who is able to punish the wicked or acquit them.

18.19.0.en: Abraham's tender heart was moved with pity for the people of wicked Sodom and Gomorrah, to give them an opportunity to repent, and he relied on a matter connected with God's justice, namely the presence of some righteous people in these two cities, and God's justice does not allow the destruction of the righteous with the wicked. So he asked God to spare the two cities if there were 50 righteous persons. Here another important truth appears, namely the importance of the life of the righteous, which becomes a cause of obtaining God's mercies not only for them but for all around them.

18.20.0.en: God accepted Abraham's intercession for the two cities of Sodom and Gomorrah and agreed to spare them if 50 righteous were found in them, and this confirms the importance of intercession with God, but sadly these fifty were not found in Sodom.

18.21.0.en: Abraham took courage with the boldness of sonship and continued his speech with God, but he did not forget his weakness as a human being, so he humbly declared that he was dust and ashes. He did not count himself great because God accepted to reveal His secrets to him, converse with him and hear his intercession, so he made a second request, that the fifty righteous be reduced by five, that is, that God spare the city if 45 righteous were found in it, and God agreed, but sadly these righteous were not found in it.

18.22.0.en: Abraham continued his intercession and made a third request, to spare the city for the sake of only 40 righteous in it, and God agreed, but sadly they were not found.

18.23.0.en: With love Abraham continued his intercession and asked God's leave that He not punish the wicked if only thirty righteous were found, and God agreed, but Abraham discovered that these thirty did not exist; then he reduced them to twenty, and God agreed, and again He did not find twenty righteous in it.

18.24.0.en: Abraham asked leave to make his last request of God in this intercession, after God had been very long-suffering toward him and had accepted all his requests, and he begged that He spare the city if ten righteous were found in it, but He did not find these righteous in it. So Abraham was ashamed of himself and became certain of God's mercy joined with His justice, so he fell silent and God vanished from before him, while he returned to his tent filled with feelings of love toward God and grief for the wicked who were about to perish.

18.24.1.en: Have pity on sinners however great their evil, and ask God to forgive them, and help them with your love so that they repent and are satisfied with God's love, so that they have no need of sin but discover its bitterness.
